question: If a sum of ₹6,70,000 is invested for a year at 2% per annum compounded half yearly, then find the compound interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the **Rate** is halved and **Time** is doubled.

New Rate = 2% ÷ 2 = 1% per half-year | Periods (n) = 1 × 2 = 2

**Effective Rate** for 2 periods = x + y + (xy/100) ⇒ 1 + 1 + (1 × 1)/100 = 2.01%

**Compound Interest** = 2.01% of ₹6,70,000 ⇒ 6,70,000 × 0.0201 = ₹13,467

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,467.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹6,70,000, **Annual Rate (R)** = 2%, **Time (T)** = 1 year.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ and CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e20e97fb9126d29155381c64aec770787f7219cd211d89d8c0f1bed726bd31f.png] 

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 2% ÷ 2 = 1%

⇒ Number of half-years (n) = 1 × 2 = 2

⇒ A = 6,70,000 × (1 + 1/100)²

⇒ A = 6,70,000 × (1.01)²

⇒ A = 6,70,000 × 1.0201 = ₹6,83,467

⇒ CI = 6,83,467 − 6,70,000

⇒ CI = ₹13,467

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,467.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is **compounded half-yearly**, the annual rate R becomes R/2 and the time T becomes 2T.

Effective Rate Formula

For two periods with rate r%, the effective percentage rate is calculated as [r + r + (r×r)/100] %.

CI vs SI for 2 Years

The difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** for 2 years is P(R/100)².
